skill.name: vet
skill.description: Run the vet CLI after small code changes to review git diffs and optional agent session history for missed implementation issues.
skill.summary: Reviews code diffs and optional conversation history after each change.
skill.author: imbue-ai

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally runs local vet commands and optional history-loader scripts that read assistant conversation files under hidden home directories. Many markdown backtick detections are false positives, but the documented command execution and transcript access are real privacy and execution risks. No prompt injection language or direct network exfiltration code was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before using history loaders, document every directory read, and default to running vet without history.
Avoid automatic pip, uv, or vet execution. Pin package versions and ask before running commands that process repository or session data.
Replace broad grep guidance with a safer session selector, or limit searches to user-approved files and redact sensitive text before processing.
Validate that --session-id starts with ses_ and contains no path separators before building filesystem paths.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Conversation History Exposure
semantic_findings.description: The skill is designed to review conversation history along with git diffs. The documented history loaders and session discovery steps can expose prompts, assistant replies, code, file paths, and secrets to vet processing.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly says vet reviews conversation history and gives loader commands for OpenCode, Codex, and Claude Code. The listed hidden session paths are known places where sensitive transcripts are stored.

semantic_findings.title: Autonomous Tool Execution Pressure
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells agents to run vet immediately after each logical unit of code changes and not wait to be asked. This can lead to unrequested command execution, especially when combined with history-loader guidance.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction is repeated in the front matter and main text. It is not malicious by itself, but it creates consent risk for commands that inspect local data.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Session Identifier Used in File Paths
semantic_findings.description: The OpenCode exporter uses the supplied session id to build a filesystem path before validating the expected ses_ format. A malformed value could cause unintended directory traversal behavior in local file reads.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The path is directly derived from user input and message ids without visible normalization or validation. Exploitability is limited because the script expects OpenCode-shaped local JSON, so confidence is medium.

content.value_statement: Code changes can drift from the user request, and tests may miss workflow issues. Vet reviews git diffs and optional session history so agents can catch problems earlier.
actual_capabilities: Runs the vet CLI after small logical code changes.
Reviews git diffs from a selected base commit.
Can include OpenCode, Codex, or Claude Code session history.
Shows commands for using vet with or without conversation history.
Documents options for model choice, confidence threshold, and output format.
Supports an agentic mode that can route analysis through local AI CLIs.
limitations: Requires the verify-everything package and vet CLI to be installed.
History loaders can read sensitive local conversation files.
Vet does not replace tests, type checks, or manual review.
Broad git diffs may include changes from other users or agents.

use_cases.title: Check Agent Code Changes
use_cases.description: Run vet after each focused implementation step to catch missed requirements or regression risks.

use_cases.title: Review Diff Against Intent
use_cases.description: Use conversation history with a git diff to compare what was requested with what was changed.

use_cases.title: Standardize Review Output
use_cases.description: Use output and threshold options to create consistent findings for pull requests or local review.

prompt_templates.title: Run Basic Vet Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check after a small code change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run vet on the current git diff without conversation history. Summarize any issues and mention whether tests are still needed.

prompt_templates.title: Review With Session Context
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review when the change depends on prior instructions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run vet with the correct session history for this conversation. Check whether the implementation matches the user request and list only actionable issues.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Review Strictness
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for noisy or large diffs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run vet with a chosen base commit and confidence threshold. Explain which findings are high confidence and which require human judgment.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Pull Request Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Run vet with a pull request friendly output format. Convert the results into a concise review summary with risks, evidence, and suggested fixes.

output_examples.input: A small refactor changes authentication middleware and updates tests.
output_examples.output: Vet reports that the middleware now skips one error path. The review recommends adding a test for expired tokens before merging.

output_examples.input: A Codex session implemented a requested UI change across several files.
output_examples.output: Vet compares the conversation request with the diff and notes that mobile spacing was not handled. It suggests checking the narrow viewport.

output_examples.input: A large branch includes work from another agent and the current task.
output_examples.output: Vet flags issues from the full diff and separates items that appear unrelated to the current session for human triage.

best_practices: Run vet after small, logical changes so findings stay focused.
Ask for consent before loading conversation history from hidden directories.
Treat vet as an extra review layer, then run the project tests.
anti_patterns: Do not run history loaders on private sessions without user approval.
Do not ignore findings solely because the change came from another session.
Do not use vet results as a substitute for compiling, testing, or manual review.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides an agent to run the vet CLI after code changes and review the resulting findings.

faq.question: Does it need conversation history?
faq.answer: No. Vet can run without history, but history can help compare the implementation with the request.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The instructions include examples for OpenCode, Codex, and Claude Code session history.

faq.question: Can it read sensitive files?
faq.answer: Yes. History-loader workflows can read hidden session directories that may contain sensitive prompts and code.

faq.question: Does vet replace tests?
faq.answer: No. The skill states that vet is not a replacement for running tests.

faq.question: Who should use it?
faq.answer: It is most useful for developers and agent operators who want frequent review of code diffs.
